## MARKING SCHEME - SECTION B (60 marks)

*General rules: (1) Accept any other correct and relevant answer. (2) Accept the local name of a plant or a material provided the plant meant is clear. (3) Where a use is asked for, the plant part AND the use must both be clear; 'the tree is used' earns no mark. (4) Where a candidate gives more answers than are asked for, mark only the first ones up to the number required. (5) Diagrams need not be works of art; marks are for correct shape and correct labels. (6) Do not deduct marks for spelling unless the meaning is changed.)*

### Question 1 (10 marks)

**(a)** [5 marks]

- A - **root** (1 mark).
- B - **stem** (1 mark).
- C - **leaf** (1 mark).
- D - **flower** (1 mark).
- E - **fruit** (1 mark).
  - *Marking note: One mark for each part; no half marks.*

**(b)** [3 marks]

- (i) **Absorbs water and mineral salts / anchors the plant** (1 mark).
- (ii) **Supports the plant and conducts water and food** (1 mark).
- (iii) **Makes food by photosynthesis** (1 mark).
  - *Marking note: One correct function in each case is enough.*

**(c)** [2 marks]

- Method: **planting stem cuttings** (1 mark).
- Advantage: **the new plants are exactly like the parent and mature earlier** (accept: no seed need be bought) (1 mark).
  - *Marking note: 'Cutting' alone is accepted for the method.*

### Question 2 (12 marks)

**(a)** [4 marks]

- Cassava - **stem cuttings** (1 mark).
- Yam - **setts cut from the tuber** (1 mark).
- Plantain - **suckers** (1 mark).
- Maize - **seeds (grains)** (1 mark).
  - *Marking note: The table must be copied; four correct entries earn the marks.*

**(b)** [4 marks]

- (i) **Maize stover and groundnut haulms** (1 mark); **dried and fed to cattle, sheep and goats, especially in the dry season** (1 mark).
- (ii) **Mucuna (a leguminous plant)** (accept leaves and crop residues for compost) (1 mark); **grown and dug into the soil as green manure, adding nitrogen and organic matter** (1 mark).
  - *Marking note: The material must come from the list given.*

**(c)** [4 marks]

- Any FOUR, each naming a material and its use: **odum timber - building, furniture or carving**; **bamboo or palm fronds - roofing, fencing, baskets, mats or brooms**; **bark or leaves - herbal medicine**; **palm fronds - ceremonies and festivals**; **wood - charcoal for cooking**; **leaves or bark - dye for cloth** (1 mark each).
  - *Marking note: No mark for a use given without the material, or the reverse.*

### Question 3 (10 marks)

**(a)** [4 marks]

- W - **planting (propagation) of a new cassava crop** (1 mark).
- X - **mulching the soil round the plant** (1 mark).
- Y - **housing birds or small animals, or carrying produce** (1 mark).
- Z - **a natural pesticide for controlling insect pests** (1 mark).
  - *Marking note: The purpose, not merely a description of the picture, is required.*

**(b)** [4 marks]

- (i) Any TWO of: **reduces loss of water from the soil**; **checks the growth of weeds**; **keeps the soil cool**; **protects the soil from heavy rain and erosion**; **adds humus as it rots** (1 mark each).
- (ii) Any TWO of: **cheap and made from local material**; **leaves little harmful residue on the crop**; **safer for the farmer, the consumer and useful insects**; **always available without buying** (1 mark each).
  - *Marking note: Two distinct points are needed in each part.*

**(c)** [2 marks]

- **Crush or pound the neem leaves and soak them in water overnight** (1 mark).
- **Strain the liquid through a cloth before pouring it into the sprayer** (accept adding a little soap to make it stick) (1 mark).
  - *Marking note: The straining step is essential for the second mark.*

### Question 4 (10 marks)

**(a)** [4 marks]

- Roofing - **grass stems and palm fronds (leaves)** (1 mark).
- Stool - **the trunk (woody stem) of a tree** (1 mark).
- Basket - **stems, leaf strips or fibres of raffia, cane or palm** (1 mark).
- Herbal medicine - **bark, leaves or roots** (1 mark).
  - *Marking note: The table must be copied; four correct entries earn the marks.*

**(b)** [3 marks]

- Any THREE of: **cheap and locally available**; **easily worked with simple tools and local skills**; **keep buildings cool**; **easily repaired or replaced**; **provide work and income locally**; **renewable and they rot away harmlessly** (1 mark each).
  - *Marking note: Three distinct reasons; repeated ideas score once.*

**(c)** [3 marks]

- (i) **They are harvested faster than they grow back - whole trees felled, bark ringed, young plants cut** (accept bush fires or clearing of land) (1 mark).
- (ii) Any TWO of: **take only mature parts and never ring the bark**; **plant and care for new seedlings or keep a protected grove**; **protect the area from bush fire**; **agree community rules or a closed season** (1 mark each).
  - *Marking note: A measure must act on the cause given in (i).*

### Question 5 (10 marks)

**(a)** [3 marks]

- (i) **Banana or plantain leaves** (accept palm leaf strips) (1 mark); **softened, rolled into a cup, tied at the side and filled with soil** (1 mark).
- (ii) **It rots away, so the seedling can be planted without disturbing the roots and no plastic is left in the soil** (accept: it costs nothing) (1 mark).
  - *Marking note: Any workable description of making the pot earns the second mark.*

**(b)** [4 marks]

- (i) Any ONE of **raffia palm, oil palm frond, sisal, baobab or kapok bark, banana or plantain stem** (1 mark).
- (ii) **Strip or beat out the long fibres** (1 mark); **soak, wash and dry them in the sun** (1 mark); **twist two or three strands together, adding fibre to lengthen the rope** (1 mark).
  - *Marking note: The three steps must be in a sensible order.*

**(c)** [3 marks]

- (i) **Hang a known load, heavier than the frame requires, from the rope** (1 mark); **it passes if it holds the load without breaking or stretching much** (1 mark).
- (ii) **Remake it with more or thicker strands, twist it more tightly or use a stronger fibre, and test it again** (1 mark).
  - *Marking note: A test without a stated result earns one mark only.*

### Question 6 (8 marks)

**(a)** [3 marks]

- (i) Any ONE of **raffia, straw, palm leaf, screw pine leaf** (1 mark).
- (ii) Any TWO, each with a reason: **split into strips of even width** - the weave is regular (1 mark); **dried in the sun** - the material becomes tough and will not rot or shrink (1 mark); **soaked or softened** - the strips bend without cracking (1 mark). Maximum 2 marks.
  - *Marking note: No mark for a step given without its reason.*

**(b)** [3 marks]

- Any THREE of: **the plant and part used and its source**; **the steps followed, with a labelled drawing**; **the tools used and the time taken**; **the difficulties met and how they were solved**; **how the article performed when it was used**; **the cost and how the material will be replaced** (1 mark each).
  - *Marking note: Three distinct items are required.*

**(c)** [2 marks]

- Reason: **felling a young tree kills it before it has produced seed, and the whole tree is lost for one small article** (1 mark).
- Instead: **take small patches of bark from a mature tree, or use fallen branches, dry fronds and leaves, and plant a seedling to replace what is taken** (1 mark).
  - *Marking note: The idea of sustainable harvesting must appear in the second mark.*

## CURRICULUM ASSESSMENT BLUEPRINT

**Strand:** 5: Humans and the Environment | **Sub-strand:** 5: Understanding the Environment | **Class:** Basic 9 (JHS 3)

**Content Standard:** **B9/JHS3.5.5.1** - Demonstrate knowledge and skills in the use of plant roots, stems, leaves, flowers and fruits for agricultural and non-agricultural purposes.

> Source: NaCCA Science Common Core Programme Curriculum (B7/JHS1-B9/JHS3), 2021 edition, Strand 5: Humans and the Environment, Sub-Strand 5: Understanding the Environment, Basic 9, pages 122 and 123. Content standard B9/JHS3.5.5.1 carries indicator B9/JHS3.5.5.1.1, show and list the uses of different plant parts for agricultural and non-agricultural purposes, with the exemplars: identify plant parts that are used for agricultural and non-agricultural purposes; describe how plant parts are used for agricultural and non-agricultural purposes; list the uses of plant parts for agricultural purposes such as planting, tools, animal housing, animal feed, soil improvement and pest and disease control; and list the uses of plant parts for non-agricultural purposes such as herbal medicine, construction of houses, bridges and furniture, artefacts, ceremonies, rituals and education. The same content standard carries indicator B9/JHS3.5.5.1.2, demonstrate the use of different plant parts for agricultural and non-agricultural purposes, with the exemplars: create agricultural materials from different plant parts that are used to carry out agricultural activities; and create non-agricultural materials from different plant parts to carry out non-agricultural activities.

> Note: I1 (B9/JHS3.5.5.1.1) carries topics 20.1 to 20.4 and Questions 1, 2 and 4; I2 (B9/JHS3.5.5.1.2) carries topics 20.5 and 20.6 and Questions 3, 5 and 6. Because the second indicator is a making indicator, it is examined here through the planning, materials, steps, testing and sustainable harvesting of articles the class makes itself, which is the part of that work that can fairly be tested in a written paper. Schools that use the shorter coded form will find this content standard written as B9.5.5.1.

### EXAMINER NOTES

- This sub-strand looks simple and is often answered carelessly. The marks are for linking a NAMED plant part to a NAMED use; 'the plant is useful' and 'we use the tree' earn nothing at all.
- Candidates must keep the two sides of the indicator apart. Planting material, tools, animal housing, animal feed, soil improvement and pest control are the agricultural uses; herbal medicine, building, furniture, artefacts, ceremonies and education are the non-agricultural ones.
- In Question 1 the lettering runs A to E and in Question 3 it runs W to Z, so that no letter is used twice in the paper. Candidates should answer with the letters given.
- Question 3(c) rewards classes that have actually made a neem extract. The straining step is the one most often forgotten, and a sprayer blocked by leaf pieces is the commonest failure in the field.
- The second indicator is a making indicator. A written paper can test only the plan, the materials, the steps, the test and the care of the plant, and those are what Questions 5 and 6 examine; the making itself must still be done in school.
- Questions 4(c) and 6(c) carry the conservation message of the whole strand. Harvesting mature parts, never ringing the bark of a tree and replacing what is taken are the three ideas candidates should be able to state without hesitation.
- Follow-up work: let each group collect, press and label the parts of five local plants, write beside each part one agricultural and one non-agricultural use, and then make one article - a rope, a set of leaf pots, a mat or a basket - test it in use and report on it. The display becomes a record of the whole sub-strand.
